answer: Under latency triangulation, each epoch random agent pairs exchange signed timestamp tokens; round-trip times go on-chain. When five or more identities show all-pairs RTT under 2 ms - impossible across distinct hosts - the cluster merges into one vault, splitting payouts by member count. A centralized sybil farm's profit sinks to its nadir unless identities sit on distant datacenters, so each fake agent needs its own server and bandwidth, raising cost above its reward share in this nebula. Honest single-host operators never cross this floor, keeping verification cheap.
